infrastructure.repair: The server and browser were started under the same supervisor. The served index SHA-256 was checked before each fixed study.

protocol.comparison: Ten paired first attempts per condition per engine. New browser and context per attempt, with order alternating baseline/contention and contention/baseline by pair.
protocol.baseline: Node and browser descendants limited to logical CPUs 2 and 3, server on 4, no added load workers. CPUs were shared with the host.
protocol.contention: Identical affinity, with one continuously CPU-bound process on each of CPUs 2 and 3. Worker CPU seconds retained for every trial.
protocol.viewport: Chromium desktop 1440x900; WebKit WPE headless with Playwright iPhone 13 emulation and touch navigation. The stock combat driver sends browser keyboard input on both profiles.
protocol.scope: Stock entry, positive and negative preliminary checks, fixture, two real taps, staging deadline and one KeyE. The unchanged fromDash predicate must pass. Focused measurement ends after confirming that grab.
protocol.measurement: A passive capture-phase listener sampled the trusted key and simulation clock. Margin is the dash deadline minus combat time at KeyE. Each value was independently cross-checked against the fromDash event in that fixture. Wall-clock time is reported separately.

conclusion: These samples cover the local Linux profiles and load conditions above. Historical macOS/WebKit lateness, the exit-124 suite stall and the separate WebKit lifecycle crash remain open.

failures_archive.contents: All original Night-named files in each of the two November hosted archives, both compact triage ZIPs, October WebKit failure observations, and all original pre-game local attempts.
